submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole is a layer-1 lexical-content detector: it sits at GELU's activation minimum (the pole's ceiling, 0.170) on abstract, relational and modifier-like content words - concept, management, development, society, culture, behaviour, specific, important, regular, teaching, and -ing forms such as doing/moving/testing - and falls to 0 (pre-activation >= 0) on every high-frequency function word (the, of, and, in, to, that, for, about, into, them, where, either) and on a large, stable set of concrete entity and measure words (model, table, window, school, map, blood, cancer, species, test, data, result, amount, output, signal, range, evidence, carbon, weather, workers, run). Which side a token falls on is fixed by the token itself rather than by context or a clean semantic class (near-synonyms split: chair fires but table does not, book fires but window does not), and the unit is retrospective - its Jacobian lens is flat (kurtosis about 3.0, no coherent promoted tokens) and 70% of its input attribution sits on the token in place - so it reads what has already been seen instead of preparing the next token.

At first light the harbor was quiet. A man walked along the pier and checked each rope twice. The ferry had left at four, and the next boat would not come until eight. He wrote the time on a small pad, then put the pad back in his coat. Gulls cried above the water. A cold wind came off the sea and pushed a loose can against the rail.

The town behind the harbor woke slowly. A baker unlocked his shop and set the bread on a wooden rack. Two fishermen carried a crate up the ramp and set it down near the door. A woman in a red coat bought a loaf and paid with coins. The baker counted the coins twice and wrote the sale on a sheet of paper. He put the paper under the counter and wiped his hands on a cloth.

At seven the bus stopped in front of the post office. The driver opened the door and waited. A nurse climbed down with a bag, and a young man with a guitar followed her. The bus pulled away and left a cloud of dust on the road.

The nurse walked to the clinic on the hill. She unlocked the door and switched on the lights. A row of seats stood against the wall, and a desk sat near the window. She set her bag on the desk and checked the papers in a folder. The first patient arrived at eight, an old man with a cough. She took his temperature and wrote the result on a card. The card went into a box with thirty more.

By noon the sky had cleared. Fishermen pulled their nets onto the dock and sorted the catch into two piles. A boy sold tea from a cart near the gate. The man from the pier bought a cup and sat on a crate. He watched the boats come in and counted them as they passed the breakwater.

In the afternoon a truck brought boxes to the shop on the corner. The driver stacked them by the door and handed a list to the owner. The owner read the list and nodded. He paid the driver, and the truck left. A dog slept in the shade of a wall. Two boys kicked a ball along the street and laughed when it rolled into a ditch.

Late that week a notice about the harbor development reached the shop by noon. The owner read the notice twice and put it on the wall near the door. He told the baker and the nurse, and they both read it too. No one spoke much about it that day.

By five the light had faded. Lamps came on along the road, and a few cars passed the harbor. The man from the pier closed his pad and walked home. He ate soup at a small table near the window and listened to the radio. A bell rang twice in the distance. He set his cup down and went to bed.
